claims.text: RHEAs are promising materials for elevated-temperature applications.
RHEAs exhibit exceptional resistance to softening and extremely high melting points.
A blended powder mixture of RHEA elements and Cu tends to segregate under equilibrium conditions because of unfavorable mixing enthalpy.
Conventional melting or casting of RHEA–Cu produces phase segregation.
Conventional melting or casting of RHEA–Cu produces an unstable microstructure.
Laser powder bed fusion or another rapid non-equilibrium method can enable large-scale synthesis of RHEA–Cu composites.
A custom non-equilibrium interatomic potential can be used to optimize rapid processing parameters for RHEA–Cu composites.
Rapid solidification limits the time available for phase separation in RHEA–Cu.
Rapid non-equilibrium processing kinetically traps a mixed RHEA–Cu state.
Kinetic trapping produces a refined microstructure with uniformly distributed phases.
The kinetically trapped phase distribution suppresses Cu-rich segregated domains.
The custom interatomic potential accurately captures RHEA–Cu mixing enthalpies.
The custom interatomic potential accurately captures segregation tendencies in RHEA–Cu.
Potential-guided optimization suppresses equilibrium phase separation and produces a uniform distribution of refractory elements and Cu.
Rapidly processed RHEA–Cu will have significantly less Cu segregation than conventionally melted or cast material.
Rapidly processed RHEA–Cu will have a stable, uniform microstructure at large scale.
Reduced Cu segregation will improve the mechanical properties of the RHEA–Cu composite.
Reduced Cu segregation will improve the irradiation resistance of the RHEA–Cu composite.
The proposed improvement depends on sufficiently rapid reaction kinetics and may fail outside the optimized processing-speed, scale, or composition range.
